correctness.rationale: All vertices of a one-halfspace clipped cube are classified. Permutation invariance and strict convexity force a unique constant-coordinate center; two exact squared-distance quadratics have minima at the two vertex-orbit means and meet at half the fractional offset. Their median minimizer gives the complete theorem and saturation. Each contact class is characterized by equality in that envelope, and orbit barycenters independently certify minimality. 333 exact-rational enumerations (103,420 vertex inequalities) corroborate but are not used as proof.

broader_coverage.reasoning: The Löwner theorem covers arbitrary rank selections of 0/1 vertices, but not genuinely fractional cap vertices and minimizes volume rather than sphere radius. Matroid minimum spheres cover integral uniform ranks; fractional caps are non-Boolean polytopes, so the central zero-one identity used there does not apply. Integer subcases are expressly excluded from novelty.

value.rationale: The exact Euclidean circumradius and center are natural, scale-sensitive geometric invariants for fractional uniform-knapsack polytopes, useful in spherical rounding. The theorem determines the full continuum of parameter values in every dimension, identifies nontrivial positive-length radius plateaus that are absent from a generic monotonicity argument, supplies sharp mixed/fractional contact transitions, and specializes consistently to the previously known integral formula.
